A git-tracked, agent-readable knowledge base for non-technical project context (domain, product, design, engineering, operations, gtm, governance). Opt-in per project; disabled when the `wiki` config group is absent.

**REQUIRED:** read `wiki-federation-model` (three-layer model, federation table, origination modes, authorship hedges), `wiki-conventions` (cross-reference protocol, before resolving a link), `wiki-page-spec` (before interpreting or validating a page's frontmatter), `wiki-page-types` (page types with their authorship and freshness defaults and per-type required fields), `wiki-configuration` (where the wiki and its reports are), `wiki-page-freshness` (before interpreting freshness behavior), and `wiki-tree-layout` (before enumerating or walking a sub-wiki's pages).
**REQUIRED:** read `wiki-write-protocol` (authorship boundary, v1 deferrals) and `wiki-authoring-spec` (the readability rules and the list of every author-facing lookup, all materialized into the wiki at `_authoring/`); read `wiki-page-spec` also before authoring a page, `wiki-page-slugs` before deriving a filename from a title, and `wiki-configuration` before `/wiki-init`.

<!-- no-required-loading -->
**Three-layer model:** Raw sources (immutable, under `_raw/`) → Federated wiki (sub-wikis in layer order: `domain/`, `product/`, `design/`, `engineering/`, `operations/`, `gtm/`, `governance/`) → Schema (agent-kit conventions). Sub-wikis opt in via `wiki.include`.
**Origination modes:** `originate` = wiki is canonical; `mirror` = external system is canonical, wiki holds summary + pointer; `link-only` = stub + pointer only.
**Authorship hedges:** `canonical` = human-authored only; `curated` = agent drafts, human approves; `derived` = agent authors from named sources. Write boundary: content pages are written only by `/wiki-ingest` (3-file set: `_raw/` copy + `source-summary` + `log.md` entry) and `/wiki-synthesize` (synthesis page + log entry), each with a disjoint write-set, and by a work-entry promotion, which writes a `curated` page's draft for approval; `/wiki-attach-artifact` adds, replaces or removes one `artifacts:` entry on a page whose type takes it; `/wiki-archive` writes only its spec-generated redirect stub; `/wiki-move` relocates a page, or a set of them, and rewrites the citations of each — beyond those it changes only the prefix a moved page's own links gain on a sub-wiki change and the order of any related list those edits disturb (`wiki-write-protocol` has the full write set); all other skills are read-only or scaffold-only.
**Cross-reference syntax:** `[[<domain>:<path>#anchor]]`; intra-sub-wiki may omit domain prefix. Broken links = lint error. Raw: `[[_raw:<path>]]`. Archive: `[[_archive:<path>]]`. Author-facing rules: `[[_authoring:<name>#<anchor>]]` — the reserved pool at `<wiki.location>/_authoring/`, framework-owned.
**Readability:** related links are ordered (intra-wiki first, then grouped by sub-wiki prefix) and pages open with a self-contained lead sentence of at most 120 chars — `wiki-authoring-spec` §Authoring for readability is canonical.
**Hierarchy:** each sub-wiki sits at one layer index (`domain` 0 → `governance` 6, declared in `federation.json`) and may reference any layer above it — a strictly lower index — and none below. The order is total and the induced grid acyclic. Applies to both `related:` frontmatter and body links; violations reported as errors by `/wiki-lint` Pass 2 when it is run (`wiki-conventions` §Cross-reference protocol says when the rules are enforced).
**Section disposition:** each template's docblock carries a `Disposition:` line governing which sections an authored page may drop. Default — keep every header; `None.` when empty, or a pointer where the content moved. Bullets — the same for each bullet of a per-block list. Variant — a shape picked up front; the `Variants:` line names the sections each keeps. A `Deviation:` label marks a departure for an external convention. A header disappears only via a Variant or a Deviation; `wiki-section-disposition` §Section disposition is canonical.
**Page state axes:** what is not true yet when a page is written sits on the axis chosen by what varies — the subject has a lifecycle (a typed `status:` with a per-type vocabulary), one declared section is not yet due (the template's `Appends:` line, and `Pending: <event>.` until it arrives, on any cadence), or the page is a register of items with their own states (per-row state in the body, with the template's `Columns:` line naming the columns an author may not trim). A declared slot closed without its event reads `None. — <reason>.`; a bare `None.` there is an error. Unresolved intent splits by ownership: an owned deferred decision goes in the `## Open questions` register, an unowned research lead in `## Follow-up leads`. `wiki-page-state` §Page state axes is canonical.
**Template propagation:** a template change is forward-looking. Pages carry the `template-version` they were created from, and only a page at its template's current version is held to its sections; older pages are not retroactively non-conformant, and migrating them is separately planned work. 0% adoption of a section or id convention a template added after its pages were written means not-yet-applicable, not violated; `wiki-template-propagation` §Template propagation is canonical.
**v1 deferrals:** threshold-based automatic archival (per-page archival runs through `/wiki-archive`).
